correctness.rationale: The selected-cell constraint is r_i+c_j≤2, and domination forbids a full omitted row and column simultaneously. Without a full line every incidence degree is at most two. A row of degree two confines all omissions to its two columns; if both columns had extra omissions in different rows, a selected cross cell would see one row omission and two column omissions. Hence the only nonmatchings are the two-edge star, the 3-cell rectangle and the 4-cell rectangle, up to transposition. With a full row there can be at most two full rows, and any other row has at most one omission. Two full rows permit no extra omission; with one full row, two extra omissions in different columns violate the cross constraint, and in the same column give a nonfull column of degree at least three. Each surviving configuration satisfies both constraints directly. The families are disjoint for m,n≥4; the matching count chooses a bijection, each three-cell block has four choices, and the slab counts choose the indicated full lines and optionally one outside cell. The maximal exponents and their coefficients give the stated minimum and multiplicity, including the tied orientations on a square. Independent code testing rook adjacency directly in branches/38eca682-5783-4f93-b41a-da41a44cf453/independent_enum.py matched complete 4×4 and 4×5 histograms and classifications (553 and 1,036 feasible sets, with 12 and 6 minimizers); the proof handles all m,n≥4.

evidence: Rook adjacency is the line graph of K_(m,n), or the unequal-alphabet two-coordinate Hamming adjacency. The complement constraint on a nonedge of the omitted incidence graph is degree sum at most two, along with no simultaneous full row and column.

value.rationale: The value is the rigidity of all feasible complements at the first capacity that permits nonmatching small components, and the resulting full size distribution. It reveals which nonextremal configurations are possible and distinguishes coincident powers arising from different shapes. This is materially stronger than the known optimum and covers a natural infinite graph family.
